title: 1994 AHSME Problem 18
statement: Triangle \(ABC\) is inscribed in a circle, and \(\angle B=\angle C=4\angle A.\) If \(B\) and \(C\) are adjacent vertices of a regular polygon of \(n\) sides inscribed in this circle, then \(n=\)

solutions.text: The angle sum gives \(9\angle A=180^\circ,\) so \(\angle A=20^\circ.\) The central angle subtending chord \(\overline{BC}\) is therefore \(40^\circ.\) Adjacent vertices of a regular \(n\)-gon subtend \(\frac{360^\circ}{n},\) so \[ \frac{360^\circ}{n}=40^\circ, \] and \(n=9.\) Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Use the triangle angle sum to find \(\angle A\)
The central angle subtending \(\overline{BC}\) is twice \(\angle A\)
